children: Asian stock markets mostly declined on Friday, mirroring losses on Wall Street as technology and artificial intelligence-related shares came under renewed selling pressure following disappointing earnings from major US tech companies. Persistent concerns about the AI trade have also weighed on Asian markets, triggering significant losses.

The Bank of Japan held its short-term policy rate unchanged at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote, maintaining borrowing costs at a 31-year high. Meanwhile, Japan’s September industrial production rebounded 2.2% M/M, unemployment edged down to 2.4% (with employment up 340,000 to 68.68M), and retail sales slowed to 2.3% YoY. Tokyo’s October core CPI cooled slightly to 2.6% Y/Y, while September housing starts dropped 2.7% Y/Y.
In Australia, Q3 producer prices rose 1.1% Q/Q, bringing annual PPI steady at 3.6%, while September private sector credit expanded 0.6% M/M.
Bitcoin fell to as low as $76,000 on Friday, hitting its lowest level since mid-September amid news of a major security breach at Binance, while gold prices declined below $4,000 per ounce.
